label: 3rd copy output (recall_idx 2) in short sequences (L=3,4), near end of copy
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and never at the delimiter or on recall_idx 0. Its main mode is the step that outputs original token 2 in short sequences: for L=3 that is the final step (t=5), where it fires about 86% of the time; for L=4 it is the second-to-last step (t=6), where it fires about 26% of the time. That one mode holds about 65% of the activation mass, and all of the top activations are L=3, t=5. Within L=4 the token identity changes how often it fires: rate is higher when the input (the token just copied) is 0/w/c/o/d, or when the previous input is c/0/q/u/b. The rest is a weak, diffuse tail near the end of the copy phase in longer sequences (e.g. L=7 t=12, L=9 t=17; about 1-5% rates). No simple positional rule captures that tail. It does not fire in the original phase or at the delimiter, and is near-silent for L=5.
